items.title: Natty Dominique Interview, 1967-11-15
items.q: Bonny Biggar, Tricky Sam, Kudu Williams, and all of the other. Who didn't come. Tricky Sam died because he died of drinking.

ctx.x: Uncle said, you don't have to play like me. I like to play like you. He said, well, we both don't have to play with each other. They were good friends. Norm Downs and Baby Dots. That was my two drummers. Cozy, cold, cozy, joy, and I don't know what.

You can get them all. All the drummers. You know, I said, I take them two drummers. One of one race, one of the other race. And when I get through pouring oil on you, brother, you never want to see Norm Downs or Baby Dots anymore. Never seen drummers. I work with good men. I work with, I haven't worked with no hands. I work with good men. Sure. We was working on 51st in Michigan. We had just left the Northside. Plantation Club? I'll never forget that as long as I live. Duke Everton and the gang came there. Bonny…
He said, you got a record of the top of my heart. I was supposed to. I know, he's nearly as tall as I am. He said, all the men have music. Sonny Gray was there.
